$comment: Source of truth for engine routing. tier: free | restricted | paid. status: planned | experimental | ready. Only experimental or ready engines may be used by skills (experimental: tell the user it is new). Optional paid services (APIs, MCP servers) are not engines: see integrations/catalog.json. checked: the date licence, stars and activity were last verified.

engines.name: motion-reel
engines.purpose: Canvas films as a pure function of time: kinetic type, UI and product motion, 2D and three.js 3D, synthesized score and sound effects, frame-exact render.
engines.requirements: Node 22+, FFmpeg, Chromium via Playwright, uv for audio scripts. GPU strongly recommended for 3D (software WebGL is far slower).

modes.name: Path-traced 3D (quality mode)
modes.purpose: Physically based light for three.js sets: real reflections and refractions, glass and caustics, soft shadows from area lights, depth of field. The same set and animation as the rasterised mode, still a pure function of time.
modes.requirements: A GPU. In the film folder: npm i three-gpu-pathtracer@0.0.27 three-mesh-bvh@0.9.17.
modes.cost: Seconds per frame on a GPU at 1080p and 256 samples (estimate, not yet measured on Apple silicon); a 30 s 60 fps film is hours, not minutes. GitHub Actions has no GPU: there it is for low-sample test frames only. Check with few samples first.
modes.notes: Uses the library's WebGL tracer, which runs in headless Chromium on every GPU. Upstream now leads with a WebGPU tracer and marks the WebGL one deprecated, hence the exact pin; the WebGPU tracer crashed on software WebGPU (SwiftShader) when tested on 2026-11-01.

engines.notes: A small canvas toolkit (4 stars on 2026-11-01), vendored so its path-traced mode and existing films keep working. Not offered by default: 3-D goes to HyperFrames + three.js or Blender. Use only when the user asks for motion-reel or for path tracing.

engines.name: HyperFrames
engines.purpose: HTML, CSS and WebGL compositions rendered to video: layouts, type, web-style motion, captions, 3-D with three.js, music-driven films with a synthesized score. The FCWM default.
engines.requirements: Node 22+, FFmpeg; Chrome is downloaded by the HyperFrames CLI on first render.
engines.notes: Run through npx at a pinned version with telemetry off (HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1). Optional GSAP animations use the GSAP Standard licence (free, custom terms with a no-compete clause, not OSI): treat as restricted when a film imports it.

engines.name: Manim Community
engines.purpose: Equations, graphs, mathematical and technical diagrams.
engines.requirements: uv (fetches Manim 0.22.1 and Python 3.12 on first use), FFmpeg. Linux also needs Pango and Cairo headers (libpango1.0-dev, libcairo2-dev). LaTeX only for MathTex.
engines.notes: Run through uv at a pinned version, not vendored. Text via Pango needs no LaTeX. Transparent output: ProRes 4444 or WebM with alpha.

engines.name: Blender
engines.purpose: Photoreal 3-D scenes: product shots, materials and light, physics-ready sets, rendered with Cycles.
engines.license_note: Free to use and your renders are yours, but Blender and any code linked to it (a film's scene.py) are GPL: share-alike if you distribute that code.
engines.requirements: uv (FCWM installs it); the bpy wheel (250-400 MB) is fetched once into uv's cache. Python 3.13 is fetched by uv.
engines.notes: Runs the official bpy module from PyPI (bpy 5.2.3 = Blender 5.2 LTS) headless through uv; no Blender app install. Cycles with a fixed seed and no adaptive sampling; GPU (Metal, OptiX, CUDA, HIP, oneAPI) when present, else CPU. CPU renders take seconds per frame at 1080p.

engines.name: Lottie / animated SVG
engines.purpose: Plays the user's Lottie or dotLottie animation (and inline animated SVG) inside a HyperFrames film, rendered to video.
engines.notes: Not a separate engine: a HyperFrames route (fcwm new --lottie). dotlottie-web pinned at 0.82.0 (934 stars, pushed 2026-10-30) instead of lottie-web (32k stars, no push since 2025-09). No Lottie or SVG file export.
engines.requirements: Same as HyperFrames; dotlottie-web is fetched from npm once into ~/.fcwm/cache.

engines.name: Remotion
engines.license_note: Free for individuals and companies up to 3 people; larger companies need a paid company licence.
